mentions.name: Hale
mentions.description: An abstract distributed systems programming language that offers fine-grained control over resources while requiring developers to express their intent to the compiler rather than declaring machinery directly. Computations are situated within a recursive graph structure incorporating message broker semantics, giving the compiler a unified view of programs across arbitrary process boundaries. Structural abstractions enable effects and formal verification syntax so architectural decisions can be checked by the compiler. The infrastructure-aware compiler configures the environments applications deploy into, with the single language covering everything from individual memory allocations to distributed fleet deployments. It is close to v1, and a fully distributed inference-as-a-service application is being built with it, matching arbitrary hardware supply against arbitrary caller demand in real time.
mentions.source_excerpt: I'm working on Hale, an abstract distributed systems language.
